correctness.rationale: For odd n>=3, m=(2^n+1)/3 is odd, the affine equation y^4+y=x^m defines a separable degree-four one-pole Artin–Schreier curve over characteristic two with genus 3(m-1)/2. The complete basis x^i y^j dx is specified by 4i+mj<=3m-5 for 0<=j<=2; distinct pole orders make it linearly independent. Direct Cartier identities yield monomial-or-zero transitions j0 i odd -> ((i-1)/2,0), j1 i even -> ((i+m-1)/2,0), j1 i odd ->((i-1)/2,2), j2 i odd ->((i-1)/2,1). With index s=4(i+1)+mj in [1,2^n], every surviving transition is modular inverse doubling, and the regular index set S is an antipodal transversal excluding exactly the pair {m,2m}. Since 2^n=-1 modulo 2^n+1, an n-fold surviving path would take s to -s, impossible: C^n=0. Explicit differential x^((m-3)/2)y dx survives n-1 maps to dx, and for n>=5 x^((m-5)/2)y dx to x²dx, proving nilpotence index n and >=2 penultimate rank. Independently enumerated full monomial basis, index antipodal property, every nonzero transition, C^n, and longest chains at odd n=3,5,7,9,11, no discrepancies.
residual_risks: Algebraically closed char2, smooth projective normalization, odd n only. Formula does not claim complete final rank or Ekedahl–Oort type. Finite checks are corroborative.

This supplies sharpness along an infinite distinguished maximal family, an antipodal explanation, and two different longest chains; it is a motivated algebraic-geometric result, not an isolated small computation.
